summary: Philistines gather at Socoh, Saul and Israel in valley of Elah, champion Goliath of Gath over 9 feet tall, bronze armor, taunts for 40 days: give man to fight me. Jesse sends David with bread and cheese to brothers, David hears taunt, asks what reward, Eliab angry, David says who is this uncircumcised Philistine to defy armies of living God? Saul says you cannot, David says lion and bear, Yahweh delivered me. Saul clothes with armor, David can't walk, takes staff, sling, five stones. Goliath curses by gods, David says you come with sword spear but I come in name of Yahweh, battle is Yahweh's. Sling stone to forehead, Goliath falls face, David takes Goliath's sword cuts head off, Philistines flee, Israel plunders.
whyItMatters: Most famous underdog story — shows Yahweh doesn't save by sword and spear, battle belongs to Lord. For zero-background, explains David's rise and paradigm of faith vs appearance.

context.author: Samuel tradition
context.setting: Valley of Elah between Socoh and Azekah, Philistine threat

outline.heading: Goliath champion taunts 40 days — no one answers
David sent with bread, hears taunt, inquires reward, Eliab angry
David to Saul — lion bear precedent, Yahweh will deliver
Saul's armor too big, staff sling five stones
Goliath curses, David: you with sword spear, I with name of Yahweh
Stone to forehead, Goliath falls, David cuts head with Goliath's sword, Philistines flee

keyVerses.text: Then David said to the Philistine, “You come to me with a sword, with a spear, and with a javelin; but I come to you in the name of Yahweh of Armies, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.
keyVerses.why: Contrast — human weapons vs divine name.

keyVerses.text: and that all this assembly may know that Yahweh doesn’t save with sword and spear; for the battle is Yahweh’s, and he will give you into our hand.”
keyVerses.why: Theological thesis — battle belongs to Yahweh.

keyVerses.text: David spoke to the men who stood by him, saying, “What shall be done to the man who kills this Philistine and takes away the reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?”
keyVerses.why: David's perspective — not just Israel vs Philistine but living God vs defiance.

questions.question: How tall was Goliath? 9 feet? Is that literal?
questions.answer: Hebrew says six cubits and a span — about 9 foot 9 inches if cubit 18 inches. Septuagint and Dead Sea Scrolls say four cubits and a span — about 6 foot 9 inches — still giant for era where average 5 foot 6, plus armor 125 pounds. Either way, he is massive. Armor description detailed: bronze helmet, coat 5,000 shekels, bronze greaves, javelin, spear like weaver's beam. Emphasis is overwhelming appearance vs shepherd boy.

questions.question: Why does David ask about reward? Is he selfish?
questions.answer: Verse 25-26 mentions king will enrich, give daughter, free father's house. David inquires — perhaps practical, perhaps makes sure others heard promise, perhaps narrator shows David not naive. More theological question he asks: who is this uncircumcised Philistine to defy armies of living God? Focus shifts from reward to God's honor, which Eliab misreads as pride.

questions.question: Why does David refuse Saul's armor and take sling and five stones?
questions.answer: Saul's armor is royal, too big, David hasn't tested it. He takes staff (shepherd), sling (shepherd weapon, not toy — deadly in skilled hands, can hit at 100+ yards, stone to forehead), five stones (maybe one for Goliath and four for brothers* or extra shots, or five is just plentiful). Shows he fights as shepherd, with tools of his vocation, trusting Yahweh who delivered from lion and bear. *Some tradition says Goliath had four brothers.

questions.question: What does 'You come with sword spear, I come in name of Yahweh' mean?
questions.answer: Contrast of weapons. Goliath's confidence is in size and metal. David's confidence is in name — reputation, character, presence of Yahweh of Armies (Yahweh Sabaoth — Lord of heavenly hosts). Battle is Yahweh's, not David's to win by skill alone, though skill is used. For reader: faith doesn't mean no sling, but sling without trust is empty.

questions.question: Why cut off head with Goliath's own sword after falling? Gross?
questions.answer: Ancient battle trophies, proof of death — brings head to Jerusalem (v54). Taking enemy's own sword shows victory complete — ironically defeated by own weapon. Philistines see champion dead and flee, Israel plunders. Story emphasizes reversal — small defeats big, weak defeats strong, through God. David later keeps sword in sanctuary? Not yet.

glossary.def: Outsider not in covenant — not just insult but theological: outside people of God defying living God's armies.
LORD of Armies/Hosts — heavenly armies, not just Israel's.
Not slingshot — leather pouch with two cords whirled and released, deadly shepherd weapon accurate to 100+ meters.
